claims.text: Comparing the highest with the lowest quintile of HEI-2015 score, the pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for CVD was 0.83 (95% CI, 0.79-0.86).
Comparing the highest with the lowest quintile of AMED score, the pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for CVD was 0.83 (95% CI, 0.79-0.86).
Comparing the highest with the lowest quintile of HPDI score, the pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for CVD was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.82-0.89).
Comparing the highest with the lowest quintile of AHEI score, the pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for CVD was 0.79 (95% CI, 0.75-0.82).
Higher dietary scores for HEI-2015, AMED, HPDI, and AHEI were statistically significantly associated with a lower risk of coronary heart disease.
Higher dietary scores for HEI-2015, AMED, HPDI, and AHEI were statistically significantly associated with a lower risk of stroke.
The inverse associations between healthy eating scores and CVD risk were consistent across most subgroups stratified by race/ethnicity and other potential risk factors.

evidence.description: Comparing the highest with the lowest quintiles, the pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of CVD were 0.83 (95% CI, 0.79-0.86) for the HEI-2015 (P for trend <.001).
Comparing the highest with the lowest quintiles, the pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of CVD were 0.83 (95% CI, 0.79-0.86) for the AMED (P for trend <.001).
Comparing the highest with the lowest quintiles, the pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of CVD were 0.86 (95% CI, 0.82-0.89) for the HPDI (P for trend <.001).
Comparing the highest with the lowest quintiles, the pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of CVD were 0.79 (95% CI, 0.75-0.82) for the AHEI (P for trend <.001).
These dietary scores were statistically significantly associated with lower risk of both CHD and stroke.
These dietary scores were statistically significantly associated with lower risk of both CHD and stroke.
In analyses stratified by race/ethnicity and other potential risk factors for CVD, the inverse associations between these scores and risk of CVD were consistent in most subgroups.

methodologies.name: Prospective cohort analysis of dietary pattern scores and CVD risk
methodologies.description: Evaluated adherence to 4 dietary pattern scores (HEI-2015, AMED, HPDI, AHEI) and calculated pooled multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for incident cardiovascular disease events.

limitations.text: Few studies have examined the associations of adherence to different dietary patterns with long-term risk of cardiovascular disease.
